companyDescription: Affordable jet-drone + C-UAS + space domain awareness · Valkyrie CCA (USMC program of record) · $100M+ in fresh contract wins this month alone · Q2 earnings Aug 5
priceNote: Down 2.55% today per live-prices.json cache (1.4h old), continuing a pullback from the $50.89 level 4 days ago and well off the 52-week high of $134. Refreshing this pick — thesis strengthened on new contract wins since the last update.
summary: Kratos just landed two fresh contracts this month — a ~$100M sole-source space domain awareness award (Jul 13) and a ~$36M air defense system award (Jul 2) — on top of a manufacturing-capacity expansion for Valkyrie (the USMC's Collaborative Combat Aircraft program of record). Q1 2026 EPS beat by 33% but the stock still fell on the print — Kratos has an unusual, real pattern of the market reacting negatively to earnings days even on strong beats, while rewarding contract-win news instead (+8.71% on late-June contract news). Named-firm targets (Jefferies $80, JPMorgan $82, Wedbush $85) average ~$82, implying ~75% upside from the pulled-back price. The Aug 5 earnings date is on the calendar, but the more reliable near-term driver here is the contract cadence, not the print itself.

catalysts.name: $100M Space Domain Awareness Contract
catalysts.description: Sole-source prime contract awarded Jul 13, 2026 for a ground-based modular space domain awareness system — puts a Kratos system into production. Real, already-announced news feeding the near-term backlog, not a forward-looking estimate.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports Aug 5, 2026. Kratos has a real, documented pattern of negative-to-mixed stock reactions on earnings days even after beats (Q1 2026: EPS beat by 33%, stock still fell 4.2-7.4% that day) — the print itself is a lower-conviction catalyst than the ongoing contract cadence, but it's the nearest dated event on the calendar.

catalysts.name: Valkyrie CCA — Manufacturing Expansion
catalysts.description: Oklahoma City campus expanded by 100,000+ sq ft (announced Jul 6) to accelerate production of Valkyrie — the USMC's Collaborative Combat Aircraft program of record — plus Firejet/Mighty Hornet IV. Signals real ramping demand, not just a design win.

risks: Kratos has an unusual, real pattern of NEGATIVE earnings-day reactions even on beats — Q1 2026 EPS beat estimates by 33% and the stock still fell 4.2-7.4% that day; the last 5 quarters averaged a -1.96% earnings-headline reaction despite consistent double-digit growth and repeated guidance raises. The Aug 5 date should not be treated as a high-conviction 'buy the beat' setup the way it would be for a typical grower

The 'aggregate consensus (20 analysts) $110' target cited in some sources is explicitly flagged as wide-dispersion, not a tight consensus — the more credible near-term number is the named-firm average (~$82) used for this report's gate
Contract-driven upside is lumpy and hard to time precisely — good for the thesis, bad for predicting exactly when the next mover hits
Stock is down sharply from its 52-week high ($134) — a level that reflected some genuine excitement that has since cooled; further multiple compression is possible if defense-budget sentiment sours
Dense macro event week (FOMC + Big Tech earnings + PCE, Jul 27-Aug 1) sits directly before the Aug 5 print, adding macro-driven volatility on top of KTOS's own idiosyncratic earnings-day pattern

estimateDates.note: Nearest dated event, but historically a lower-conviction catalyst than contract news for this specific stock
The real near-term driver — 2 awards totaling ~$136M already landed this month alone

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed at 3.50-3.75%; defense/DoD program spending is policy-driven and largely rate-insensitive. Kratos's near-term drivers (contract cadence, Valkyrie ramp) are decoupled from the rate cycle.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE at 3.4% YoY (May) doesn't materially change defense procurement budgets, which are set through the appropriations process, not monetary policy.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: LOW-MEDIUM. Defense names are typically more insulated from a hawkish-Fed macro tape than high-multiple tech, though the stock's own valuation (already well off its 52-week high) carries some multiple-compression risk in a genuine risk-off week.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk LOW — the contract-cadence thesis and Valkyrie ramp are policy/program-driven, not rate-driven. The Aug 5 earnings date sits right after the dense Jul 27-Aug 1 FOMC/earnings/PCE week, but Kratos's own earnings-day behavior (often negative even on beats) is a bigger idiosyncratic risk than the macro backdrop here.
